[quote=the_crystalline_empire;60575572][b]July 16, 2025: Cyberattack[/b]
Breaking!:
A major cyber-attack has struck major Tallislandic government facilities and websites, potentially knocking them offline for several hours, the cyber attack has targeted crucial functions of the main government and would seek to destabilise morale among members of the current standing government of Tallisland. The government of Thýven has extended plausible deniability, denying the attacks came from their forces, instead blaming a group known as The Republicans of Elseyr, a moderate militia connected "unofficially" to the Bank of Tharkønn. 
------------------------

[spoiler=Two can play at that game]
DSA Cyberdefense

The cyberattacks now being carried out against the Tallisland government would find that since the country's accession to the EDU, the Republic's Digital Security Agency (DSA) had made significant progress in fortifying Tallislands critical digital infrastructure. Many government facilities that the cyberattacks targeted, particularly those related to defense, had been air gapped by the DSA. The complete cut off of these systems from the larger net would make it extremely difficult for them to be accessed by cyberweapons. Throughout the cyberattacks critical government infrastructure including C2 nodes and weapons systems remain online. 

Private sector contractors at work in Tallisland combined with the DSA would work towards defending the countries digital infrastructure. Intrusion detection systems running constantly would allow the DSA to find a rapid spike in suspicious activity quickly after the first cyberweapons were deployed. Using the advanced SIEM models employed by the Republik, the clear fingerprints of a cyebrweapon at work were quickly detected by the agency. Firewalls installed by private Republik contractors quickly segment the sites under attack into isolated sections, quickly stemming the tide of the cyber attacks as well as blocking DDOS requests. 

Honeynets mimicking real Tallislander government systems, data and networks work to attract cyberattacks toward them to allow the DSA to study the cyberweapon utilized in the attack including the zero day exploits utilized in order to quickly patch them and deny future access. Quickly, after the exploits used to access the systems are patched the websites and systems used by the Tallislander government come back online within minutes. Backups and redundancies allow the DSA to rapidly restore the systems to their original state. 

On the Offensive 

If the government of Thyven wanted to play a game of proxies then the Republik would do the same. DSA contractors had over the years purchased millions of dollars worth of zero day exploits. Using the inherent flaws within software, the proxies of the DSA would work to worm their way into Thyven systems. A wide range of delivery systems from removable media to network service requests to third party updates and more occurring thousands and thousands of times across Thyven cyberspace would rapidly expand the vector of attack. Once inside the system the cyberweapons work to discreetly blend into normal traffic, only moving when traffic is naturally high as well as utilizing remote code execution to avoid detection. Additionally through encryption they mask themselves as typical network traffic while being anything but. Deleted logs and modified timestamps makes tracking them even harder than finding theyre there in the first place. 

Now, if within, the programs work to expand their privileges. RCE zero-days allow them to continue to stack their authorizations and privileges as they move laterally through the networks. 

Once they have accomplished this the payloads execute.

Almost every critical piece of Thyvens military infrastructure is attacked. Even the air gapped systems of the Thyven defense forces arent safe. Using human based removable media as well as infected firmware, the DSAs proxies work to plant themselves into Thyvens defense apparatus. Quickly they work to publish massive amounts of classified data onto the open internet for all to see: troop movements, official specs, government documents and anything they can get their hands on. Targeting systems are hit with ghost targets while the integrated air defense systems operating systems are under attack. For the autonomous systems of the defense forces of Thyven the DSA works to insert massive amounts of false data to poison their ability to function. Once access is gained to the military's communications massive DDOS attacks ensue to kill the defense forces abilities to communicate. A flood of requests across government and military communications works to slow down the digital systems until they become nearly unusable. 

However, the attacks by proxy groups aren't just limited to the military. Once inside the Thyven financial sector they begin to wreak havoc. Once their RCE zero-day exploits allow them to access higher and higher authorizations they begin the mass deletion and transferring of funds from financial institutions with the purpose of causing chaos in financial markets and triggering bank runs. On the stock market, the cyberattacks start to manipulate prices for commodities, securities and various financial instruments with the purpose of causing huge price swings and triggering sell-offs across the Thyven market. Within the energy sector cyberattacks are relentless. Hitting operator workstations, utility IT and control systems to overload management parts and open breakers, the DSAs proxies aim for a full shutdown of the Thyven electrical grid. At every point from energy production to its distribution through the grid, cyberweapons work to wreak havoc and plunge the entire country into darkness. In hospitals across the country, the cyberattacks move to wipe patient records, shut down medical equipment and take down the digital equipment that the staff relies on. 

Now, however, the cyberweapons would also work to create massive lasting damage in Thyvens digital infrastructure. Logic bombs or splices of code that trigger mass deletions or work to shut down networks are planted in the millions into infected cyberspace. Able to lie dormant until triggered, they would be extremely hard to remove, especially as they blend into non-malicious code. Removing them could well take billions and billions of dollars, years of effort and take down critical infrastructure. 
[/spoiler]

[i]Meteorologists at the Weather & Radar Service office in Tenahaston spent the entire afternoon of July 22nd, 2026, monitoring scattered thunderstorms across the region. Theyve been on high alert ever since a Tornado Watch was issued for most of Gourcovencia Province until 20:00 Eastern Elseyr Time. Wind shear, coupled with instability in the atmosphere, has given way to a potent environment for the development of multiple tornadoes. Besides a few spin-ups that have been radar-confirmed in open fields, the day has been uneventful, with many wondering if today was really a Moderate Severe Weather daysome even less concerned about the thunderstorms.
However, as the day goes on and the storms enter a more favorable atmosphere, a certain supercell roughly eighty kilometers west of the office (currently only warned under a Severe Storm Alert) catches the attention of the meteorologists. A scan comes ina hook starts to form. Another scanvelocity shows a tightening area of rotation. One moreand now a blue dot appears on the correlation coefficient. Scan after scan, the storm strengthens and intensifies until, at 15:57 EET, loud, robotic beeping noises envelop the western fringe of the Tenahaston Metropolitan Area.[/i]
